header_summary:
A new Bitcoin Improvement Proposal draft, available at [this GitHub link](https://github.com/jeanpablojp/bips/blob/witness-inclusion-proofs/bip-witness-inclusion-proofs.md), seeks to standardize transaction inclusion proofs using wtxid by consolidating multiple independent approaches. The draft defines two proof formats, details explicit validation steps, addresses historical anomalies such as those in block 481823, and proposes mitigation strategies for lightweight client limitations, inviting community feedback to ensure broad interoperability [Source](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/C899B11E-4971-4AAF-8BA3-81EBAFBF7739@jeanpablo.jp/T/#u#meb2b2f0670b30c170d2e4099b87537be5c558448).

Recent security updates have been released to address a medium severity vulnerability in Bitcoin Core, with fixed versions [31.3](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/20/release-31.3/) and [30.5](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/20/release-30.5/) now available; version 32.1 already includes the fix. Further details can be found in the [official security advisory](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/20/disclose-orphan-inv-stall/), and users of unsupported versions are urged to upgrade to maintain operational security [Source](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/66d5e3d6-5a16-49ba-b7cc-442eb73252a5n@googlegroups.com/T/#u#m70332795a64238e4a0b1d6aae13c31f1c4f93ce8).

Bitcoin Core versions [30.5](https://bitcoincore.org/bin/bitcoin-core-30.5/) and [31.3](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/bitcoin-core-v31-3-released/3110) introduce substantial bug fixes, performance improvements, and updated translations, with enhancements in networking—such as unique transaction inventory processing—and continuous integration. Contributors like fanquake, Greg Sanders, and willcl-ark are acknowledged for their roles, while migration guidance and backward compatibility with older wallets are emphasized.

Discussions on UTXO snapshot proofs highlight the complexity of transitioning to blake2s and recommend publishing authoritative Merkle hashes, leveraging modular tools and alternative hash functions for scalability. Projects such as [Flock](https://github.com/succinctlabs/flock) and [Binius64](https://github.com/binius-zk/binius64) are proposed for performance gains, advocating for iterative development from manageable snapshots toward genesis proofs [Source](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/a-stark-proof-of-bitcoins-utxo-set-at-block-972-500-with-circuits-proven-in-lean/3070/7).

The btc-toolkit utility ([code reference](https://github.com/devdavidejesus/btc-toolkit)) enables transaction verification via Esplora or Mempool APIs without reliance on a full node, implementing rigorous checks against CVE-2017-12842 and providing a nuanced assessment of proof-of-work. Suggestions include calibrating verification thresholds to evolving network conditions and integrating cumulative header verification, while recognizing the inherent limitations of SPV-style trust models [Source](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/checking-transaction-inclusion-against-an-untrusted-explorer-api-how-much-proof-of-work-is-enough/3113).

recent_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Witness Transaction Inclusion Proofs
recent_posts.summary: - A draft proposes standardizing transaction inclusion proofs using wtxid, consolidating various independent implementations.  - Two formats for inclusion proofs are described, with differences in size and compatibility discussed.  - Explicit segwit activation input and additional validation measures are introduced to ensure secure verification.

recent_posts.title: Bitcoin Core security advisory for an easily discoverable vulnerability
recent_posts.summary: - Two new releases resolve a medium severity security vulnerability for supported software versions.  - The official security advisory and additional details are available via provided online resources.  - Users on version 29.x should urgently upgrade for continued system safety and reliability.

recent_posts.title: Bitcoin Core v30.5 Released
recent_posts.summary: - Bitcoin Core v30.5 delivers bug fixes, performance improvements, and expanded translation support for users.  - Installation requires a full shutdown of previous versions and follows detailed instructions for each operating system.  - Networking and workflow upgrades, along with community contributions, advance efficiency and collaboration in this release.

recent_posts.title: A STARK proof of Bitcoin's UTXO set at block 972,500, with circuits proven in Lean
recent_posts.summary: - Publishing authoritative Merkle hashes for snapshots enhances trust and supports independent verification of data.  - Efficient, purpose-built tools and improved data structures help address complexity and performance challenges.  - Iterative development with incremental snapshots is recommended to ensure reliable proofs from genesis are feasible.

recent_posts.title: Checking transaction inclusion against an untrusted explorer API: how much proof of work is enough?
recent_posts.summary: - btc-toolkit verifies transaction and block data from APIs, applying extensive security and integrity checks.  - It assesses proof-of-work for headers, with limitations on chain position verification and evolving difficulty.  - Additional methods and safeguards are explored, but API reliance leaves consensus and chain trust unresolved.

recent_posts.title: Bitcoin Core v31.3 Released
recent_posts.summary: - Bitcoin Core version 31.3 provides bug fixes, performance improvements, and updated multilingual translations.  - Users should follow specific upgrade steps, with compatibility generally maintained for older wallet formats.  - Major updates include unique transaction processing, better integration tools, and acknowledgments for contributors.

active_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Stale Tip Relay
active_posts.summary: - The `staletip` proposal enables nodes to share stale tip data, improving network observability and diagnostics.  - Only tips within 1000 blocks and up to 20 compressed headers are shared to manage data efficiency.  - Nodes maintain a cache of up to 10 recent tips, encouraging feedback to refine the feature further.

active_posts.title: RFC: Two years of BIP Editing, time for some new faces?
active_posts.summary:
- The BIP Editors made significant contributions, processing 596 pull requests and publishing 42 new BIPs.
- Improvements included revised processes, document updates, CI script enhancements, and repository cleanups.
- A proposal suggests appointing three dedicated editors to ensure sustainable management and progress.

active_posts.title: Quantum Landmines and Vulnerable Coin Auctions
active_posts.summary: - Quantum landmines and staked auctions use incentives and cryptography to protect legacy coins.  - Sats auctions employ escalating bids, deterring attackers and potentially allowing owners to recover value.  - No single optimal design exists, so adaptive, incentive-driven strategies remain necessary against quantum threats.

active_posts.title: Unspendable keys in descriptors
active_posts.summary:
- Miniscript and taproot integration in Bitcoin Core introduces challenges in generating unspendable keys for wallets.
- Methods include using fixed or random-chaincode xpubs and recycling entropy from descriptors or taptrees.
- Each approach involves trade-offs regarding uniqueness, indistinguishability, user experience, and hardware compatibility.

active_posts.title: Bounds on chain length with BIP-54 timewarp fixes
active_posts.summary: - Timewarp attack rules restrict block timestamps to prevent manipulative behaviors that threaten blockchain integrity.  - Mathematical modeling shows these rules establish a computable upper bound on blockchain growth under consensus rules.  - A formal proof confirms these findings, providing reliable guidance for safeguarding timestamp-based consensus mechanisms.

active_posts.title: Propagation Delay and Mining Centralization: Modeling Stale Rates
active_posts.summary: - Block propagation times influence miners' revenue and can lead to increased mining centralization.  - Larger pools benefit more due to higher chances of winning block races in propagation delays.  - Simulations show that reducing propagation delays can promote fairness and reduce centralization in mining.

today_in_history_posts.title: BIP159 - NODE_NETWORK_LIMITED service bits, extendability
today_in_history_posts.summary: - The BIP159 proposal enables pruned nodes to serve a limited number of historical blocks.  - Flexibility to increase prune depth and counter fingerprinting risks could be offered as opt-in.  - Improvements suggested include better references and clarification of the 288-block limit and purpose.

today_in_history_posts.title: Directionality of the transaction fees
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Setting different fees for sending and receiving can help manage channel balance.  - Adjusting fees dynamically may prevent channels from becoming unbalanced and reduce risks.  - Automatic fee regulation by lightning network applications is suggested as an ideal solution.

today_in_history_posts.title: Thoughts on scaling and consensus changes (2023)
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Scalability for mass Bitcoin adoption relies on 50,000 diverse off-chain entities and innovative coinpool solutions.  - Auditable, interconnected banks and optimized Layer 2 protocols are prioritized over increasing block size.  - Emphasis is placed on proactive security measures, regulatory compliance, and robust infrastructure for safe operation.
